newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to higher.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.200 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while pork bellies were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent a lb higher, livestock analysts said.

Nearby hog futures were expected to climb following a sharp upward reversal in wholesale pork prices and continued concern over bitter cold weather and its impact on Midwest hog marketings and slaughter operations, analysts said.
Pork cutout values turned up after recently falling to lowest prices levels since mid April.
However, less-than-expected corn stocks estimated by USDA early Friday morning could pressure deferreds, traders said.
The aparent increased corn usage could mean that hog numbers may be larger than estimated in the last Hogs and Pigs report, some analysts said.

Pork bellies were seen showing strength from projections of weather-reduced hog slaughter rates. The wintry weather is not only cutting hog runs but is also keeping some packing plants from operating, some sources said.
However, carryover technical pressure and expectations for increased hog runs and kills when temperatures moderate, may temper gains, they added.
